answer.says: You are too generous, Sunil. The samosa was the better part of the bargain; do not let me leave you at a loss. I will take the cup, but I insist on paying for the whole, or at least the biscuit to go with it. It is the nature of the exchange that it be balanced.
answer.thought: The system of needs usually operates on cold arithmetic, but here is a moment of particularity that resists the universal rule. Sunil’s refusal to take payment for the samosa is a gesture that disturbs the simple calculation of value; it is a small act of freedom within the necessity of trade. I must not let the debt remain unpaid, for it would bind me in a way I do not wish, yet I must accept the chai as a gift of the moment.
